_comment: ADR 0027 — input bundle: WASD with first-person + third-person variants. Rules: 4 world-frame (top_down_3d only) + 4 camera-relative for FPS / third-person (both use velocity_add_relative driven by state.facing) + 4 camera-relative iso (isometric_3d, facing=π/4 fixed). 2026-05-19 update: third_person_3d moved from world-frame to camera-relative — mouse-look rotates the player + camera together, so W should walk in player's facing direction (not world-north), same as FPS. Per-game rules.json splices via {$include: '@lib.input_bundles.wasd_with_fp_variant.rules'}. Action declarations under `actions` are FOR DOCUMENTATION; per-game ui/input.json still authors its own action list (the canonical InputMap declarations).

actions.name: stop_x
actions._doc: Engine-injected when neither move_east nor move_west is held. Per-axis idle: zero only the x component. Lets W+A (NW) → release A → keep W behavior work correctly: stop_x zeros x (was -3 from A), move_north sets y=-3, result (0, -3) = pure north.

actions.name: stop_y
actions._doc: Engine-injected when neither move_north nor move_south is held. Same per-axis idle pattern.

actions.name: stop
actions._doc: LEGACY full-idle stop. Engine-injected when no movement key is held AND stop_action_on_idle='stop'. New games should use stop_x + stop_y (per-axis); kept for backwards-compat.

rules._comment: World-frame WASD — fires when camera is NOT first_person_3d. W=north regardless of player facing. Spliced into game's rules.json rules array. Per-axis pattern (added 2026-05-10): each directional rule sets ONLY its own axis. Engine's velocity_set preserves the OTHER axis when the field is omitted, so W+D = north + east diagonal works (each rule contributes one axis; combined velocity is (3, -3) at 45°). With both axes set per rule, last-writer-wins broke diagonals.

STOP_X — engine queues stop_x when neither move_east nor move_west is held (per-axis idle, world.gd::_poll_input). Zeros only the x component — preserves y so a still-held W/S keeps working. Gated to world-frame cameras only: camera-relative WASD (FP/iso) uses velocity_add_relative which auto-resets per tick; running stop_x there would WIPE the camera-relative x component when only one of forward/strafe is held.
STOP_Y — mirror of STOP_X for the y axis (north/south). Same world-frame gate.

Full-idle STOP — fires when no movement key is held AND stop_action_on_idle='stop'. Both world-frame AND camera-relative cameras use this for snap-to-stop (no camera filter needed). For camera-relative WASD: when no keys held, velocity_add_relative doesn't fire, so this rule's velocity_set is what zeroes the leftover velocity. For world-frame: redundant with stop_x+stop_y but harmless.

Camera-relative WASD — fires when camera IS first_person_3d. Engine's velocity_add_relative reads actor.state.facing (mouse-driven by _camera_first_person_3d's _drain_mouse_facing) and rotates forward/strafe into world XZ. The effect AUTO-RESETS velocity on the FIRST add per sim-tick (ADR 0048): old-tick velocity never carries over, so mouse-turn-mid-walk doesn't drift; multiple input rules in the SAME tick accumulate (W+D → forward+strafe diagonal). The full-idle stop rule (lib_wasd_stop) handles snap-to-zero when no key is held.

ADR 0040 — Camera-relative WASD for isometric_3d. Player presses W → moves where the camera is 'looking forward' (NW in world for SE-camera-looking-NW). facing=π/4 = 45° rotates the (forward, strafe) basis to align with the camera's XZ projection. velocity_add_relative auto-resets per tick (ADR 0048) so W+D both held → contributions sum to world-N (pure -Z) → projects to screen-up-right. Speed clamp via state.max_speed normalizes the diagonal sum to walking speed.
